name: Opus-fleet price momentum
strategy: Concentrated long-only US price momentum: hold only leaders above both their 50- and 200-day averages (LLY, MCK, TMO, MSFT) with 10% stops, and keep 57% cash while SPY trades below its 50-day average.
reassessment_note: MRNA stopped out on 11-13 (-17% realized) and its 9% sat in cash. I pulled one year of daily closes (Yahoo chart API) for SPY, my three remaining legs and about 110 large caps. SPY closed 754.37 on 11-13, below its 50-day (764.4) but above its 200-day (731.9), so the risk-off filter still holds and gross stays at 43%. LLY, TMO and MSFT are all still above both averages, so they stay at the same weights. MSFT has the weakest margin (523.9 vs a 50-day of 519.0, -2.9% over 1 month), and its 10% stop is the exit if the trend breaks. The 9% that MRNA freed goes to McKesson. Of the names screened above both averages, it has the best combined 3-, 6- and 12-month momentum among large caps outside the speculative tail: +28% over 3 months, +45% over 6 and +31% over 12. That fits the healthcare and defensive leadership the screen shows (MCK, CAH, REGN, GILD, ABBV). A web search confirmed the fundamental backdrop: fiscal Q2 was reported on 11-04, management said market fundamentals are stable, and the CVS distribution contract runs through 2032. I did not choose APP even though its 1-month return is higher, because its 12-month return is negative and it is a high-beta name in a tape where SPY is below its 50-day. The only cost is a 9% buy at about 2bps. The unchanged legs re-enter at the 11-16 close, which resets their stop basis.

positions.thesis: This is the strongest trend in the book. LLY closed 1443.5, far above its 50-day (1241) and 200-day (1109), and is up 15% over 1 month, 22% over 3 and 44% over 6. It keeps the largest weight as the momentum leader, and a 10% stop protects the gain.

This replaces the stopped-out MRNA at the same 9%. MCK closed 1102.8, above its 50-day (955) and 200-day (874), and is up 28% over 3 months, 45% over 6 and 31% over 12. Drug distribution leadership is backed by the fiscal Q2 report (11-04) and the CVS contract renewed through 2032. It is a lower-beta momentum name than MRNA, which suits a market where SPY is below its 50-day. A 10% stop caps the risk.

TMO closed 700.2, above its 50-day (671) and 200-day (555), and is up 20% over 3 months and 60% over 6. It has been flat for a month (+0.5%) but the trend is intact, so I hold it at 10% with a 10% stop.

MSFT closed 523.9, just above its 50-day (519.0) and well above its 200-day (441), and is up 9% over 3 months and 24% over 6. It is the weakest leg on short-term momentum (-2.9% over 1 month), so it stays at 10% rather than adding. The 10% stop is the exit if the AI-trade rotation keeps going.
